title: Dependency unblock SLA and transit-time playbook for cross-team roadmaps
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Roadmap items that depend on work from other teams (Eng/Design/Security/Infra) frequently exceed expected handoff times; missing SLAs and inconsistent escalation behavior cause scope slippage, unclear ownership, and OKR friction.

Proposal: Define a lightweight "transit-time" metric (time from dependency being flagged to first actionable acknowledgement by the owning team) and an associated three-tier unblock SLA with automated escalation. Ship: (1) a dependency ingestion flow in Linear that tags roadmap tickets, (2) instrumentation and dashboards in Console/Datadog for transit-time & backlog, (3) an operational playbook describing ownership, canary windows, and compensating actions for high-impact blockers.

Goals: Reduce average transit-time from 4.2 business days to <= 24 hours for P0/P1; establish deterministic escalation paths for >48 hour blocked dependencies; provide crediting rules so teams that unblock third-party blockers are recognized in velocity/OKR reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Linear dependency fields created: dependency_flagged_at, owning_team, onboarding_ack_at and escalation_state
Transit-time metric computed and visible in Console with rollout to all roadmap-level tickets
Datadog dashboard shows 7, 30, 90-day rolling percentiles (p50/p90/p99) of transit-time by team and label
Automated Slack escalation bot posts to #roadmap-escalations after 48 hours for P0/P1 with link to runbook
Crediting rules implemented in roadmap reporting: unblock events are attributed and exported to OKR spreadsheets
Playbook published to Confluence with example escalations and a retro template
implementation_notes: Product: define dependency schema and mapping to OKR tags; coordinate with PM tooling owners
Engineering: add Linear webhook to enrich tickets on dependency creation; implement webhook consumer to write timestamped events to events-service
Design: produce a small UI affordance in Console ticket view to show current transit-time and last escalation
Security: sign-off on webhook auth and Slack bot scopes; ensure audit log entries for auto-escalations
Infra: ensure events-service retention 90d and index keys for team and ticket id to support dashboards

risks: Teams may not consistently tag dependencies causing gaps in telemetry; mitigation: use default tagging heuristics and weekly audit
Escalation noise if SLA thresholds are misconfigured — start with conservative windows and tune for p90
Crediting may distort velocity if not aligned with team incentives — tie unblock credits to explicit OKR outcomes not sprint points
